database: Lace engines with block anchors, classes, settings and hidden blocks require migration 0009_content_block_envelope. It is additive: it adds the nullable content_blocks.anchor and class_name columns, hidden (default 0) and settings_json (default '{}') plus a partial unique index on (snapshot_id, anchor), without a table rebuild or backfill, so existing blocks read as visible without an anchor or class and with empty settings. Back up first: an older engine starts against the migrated database but would deliver hidden blocks publicly and reset block envelopes on save, so rolling back the API and admin once anchors, classes, settings or hidden blocks exist requires restoring that backup.

Compose (Node SQLite) for 0009: stop dispatch and the API with docker compose stop api dispatcher, back up the stopped database by copying the whole .lace/data directory, set the new images in .env, run pnpm db:migrate, then pnpm content:sync, then start again with pnpm dev:api or pnpm prod:start.

Cloudflare (D1) for 0009: back up first (pnpm exec wrangler d1 export <database-name> --remote --output <backup-file>, or record a Time Travel restore point), run pnpm exec lace cloudflare preflight and pnpm exec lace db migrate --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env and pnpm exec lace content sync --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, then deploy the rebuilt Worker with pnpm exec wrangler deploy --config worker/wrangler.jsonc. Local simulated data: stop cf:dev and run pnpm cf:db:migrate.

Lace engines with per-entry SEO require migration 0008_content_snapshot_seo. It is additive: it adds the nullable content_snapshots.seo_json column without a table rebuild or backfill, so existing entries, publications and media are unchanged. Older engines keep starting against the migrated database, so rolling back the API and admin works without restoring; SEO values saved meanwhile stay stored but unused.

Compose (Node SQLite) for 0008: stop dispatch and the API with docker compose stop api dispatcher, back up the stopped database by copying the whole .lace/data directory, set the new images in .env, run pnpm db:migrate, then pnpm content:sync, then start again with pnpm dev:api or pnpm prod:start.

Cloudflare (D1) for 0008: back up first (pnpm exec wrangler d1 export <database-name> --remote --output <backup-file>, or record a Time Travel restore point), run pnpm exec lace cloudflare preflight and pnpm exec lace db migrate --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env and pnpm exec lace content sync --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, then deploy the rebuilt Worker with pnpm exec wrangler deploy --config worker/wrangler.jsonc. Local simulated data: stop cf:dev and run pnpm cf:db:migrate.

Lace engines with global models require migration 0007_content_model_global_kind. It rebuilds the content_models table to accept the new global kind and keeps every model, entry and publication; on Node SQLite the migrator suspends foreign keys on its own connection and verifies them before restoring enforcement, on D1 it runs as one batch with deferred foreign keys. Back up first: older engines keep starting against the migrated database only while no global exists, so rolling back the API and admin after configuration sync created a global requires restoring that backup.

Compose (Node SQLite) for 0007: stop dispatch and the API with docker compose stop api dispatcher, back up the stopped database by copying the whole .lace/data directory, set the new images in .env, run pnpm db:migrate, then pnpm content:sync, then start again with pnpm dev:api or pnpm prod:start.

Cloudflare (D1) for 0007: back up first (pnpm exec wrangler d1 export <database-name> --remote --output <backup-file>, or record a Time Travel restore point), run pnpm exec lace cloudflare preflight and pnpm exec lace db migrate --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env and pnpm exec lace content sync --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, then deploy the rebuilt Worker with pnpm exec wrangler deploy --config worker/wrangler.jsonc. Local simulated data: stop cf:dev and run pnpm cf:db:migrate.

Lace engines with schema evolution and media metadata require migrations 0005_content_model_structure and 0006_media_descriptive_metadata. Both are additive ALTER TABLE statements: 0005 adds the content_models structure baseline columns that configuration sync fills, and 0006 adds the optional media alt, caption and focal point columns. Existing content and media are unchanged. Older engines keep starting against the migrated database, so rolling back the API and admin works without restoring.

Compose (Node SQLite) for 0005 and 0006: stop dispatch and the API with docker compose stop api dispatcher, back up the stopped database by copying the whole .lace/data directory, set the new images in .env, run pnpm db:migrate, then pnpm content:sync, then start again with pnpm dev:api or pnpm prod:start.

Cloudflare (D1) for 0005 and 0006: back up first (pnpm exec wrangler d1 export <database-name> --remote --output <backup-file>, or record a Time Travel restore point), run pnpm exec lace cloudflare preflight and pnpm exec lace db migrate --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env and pnpm exec lace content sync --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, then deploy the rebuilt Worker with pnpm exec wrangler deploy --config worker/wrangler.jsonc. Local simulated data: stop cf:dev and run pnpm cf:db:migrate.

Lace engines with invitations and password recovery require migration 0004_account_tokens. It is additive: it adds the invitations and password_reset_tokens tables (token digests only) and leaves existing users, sessions and content unchanged. Older engines keep starting against the migrated database, so rolling back the API and admin works without restoring; invitation and reset links issued meanwhile stop working.

Compose (Node SQLite) for 0004: stop dispatch and the API with docker compose stop api dispatcher, back up the stopped database by copying the whole .lace/data directory, set the new images in .env, run pnpm db:migrate, then start again with pnpm dev:api or pnpm prod:start.

Cloudflare (D1) for 0004: back up first (pnpm exec wrangler d1 export <database-name> --remote --output <backup-file>, or record a Time Travel restore point), run pnpm exec lace cloudflare preflight and pnpm exec lace db migrate --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, then deploy the rebuilt Worker with pnpm exec wrangler deploy --config worker/wrangler.jsonc. Local simulated data: stop cf:dev and run pnpm cf:db:migrate.

Lace 0.1.0-alpha.3 engines require migration 0003_site_build_outcomes, which 0.1.0-alpha.2 engines lack. It rebuilds site_builds for the seven-status build history and adds provider tracking fields; former running rows become accepted, and on D1 succeeded rows without a provider ID also become accepted because a deploy hook never proved publication.

Compose (Node SQLite): stop dispatch and the API with docker compose stop api dispatcher, back up the stopped database by copying the whole .lace/data directory, set the 0.1.0-alpha.3 images in .env, run pnpm db:migrate, then start again with pnpm dev:api or pnpm prod:start (the migrate service also applies pending migrations on start).

Cloudflare (D1): back up first (for example pnpm exec wrangler d1 export <database-name> --remote --output <backup-file>, or record a D1 Time Travel restore point with pnpm exec wrangler d1 time-travel info <database-name>), run pnpm exec lace cloudflare preflight and pnpm exec lace db migrate --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env before deploying the rebuilt Worker with pnpm exec wrangler deploy --config worker/wrangler.jsonc. Local simulated data: stop cf:dev and run pnpm cf:db:migrate.
Downgrading to 0.1.0-alpha.2 after this migration requires restoring the backup, because older engines reject the new build statuses.
configuration: Template 0.36.0: Gallery v4 reusable list layouts. No database migration is needed. Back up content/site, upgrade compatible engine, admin, CLI and site packages, then run lace add block gallery --site site --dry-run and review component plus ListLayout.css together. Resolve conflicts using --write-new and manual merges; never overwrite edited user files. Remove old unlayered Gallery display/columns rules, retain 1rem spacing with --lace-list-gap and keep image/theme CSS. Increment model versions structurally including Gallery, deploy matching definition/renderer, then run normal content sync. Identity migration 4 retains content/settings and fills missing grid/true/auto defaults; migrations 2/3 remain. Rerun interrupted sync. Validate layouts, publish and build. After sync, rollback requires the pre-upgrade content backup and matching older code/site sources; no automatic down-migration. See docs/lace-astro-site.md.

Template 0.35.0: alpha.7 release coordinates and image delivery. All managed package dependencies, image defaults and guide commands select 0.1.0-alpha.7. Set LACE_API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/api:0.1.0-alpha.7 and LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/builder:0.1.0-alpha.7 in the user-owned .env. Upgrade engine/admin, site dependencies and API/builder images together. No new SQL migration since alpha.6; older pending migrations remain explicit. Generate the target with the same site mode/path and Cloudflare selection. Review nginx, Compose and Pages workflow conflicts; .env, configuration, site source and operator settings stay user-owned. Before content sync, update or merge image/gallery/hero registry components and site lightbox/link CSS, add sharp and image: laceImageConfig(env), then raise affected model versions. Sync migrates image/gallery blocks to versions 4/3; older components reject those schemas. Restore matching database/configuration/media/site-source backups to roll back synchronized content. See docs/lace-astro-site.md and docs/lace-operations.md; reinstall dependencies and rebuild the Worker/site.

Template 0.34.0: image links. The built-in image block moves to version 4 and gallery to version 3, each with an optional Link (a safe URL field) on the image block and on every gallery item; a linked image opens its link in the same tab instead of the lightbox, and images without a link keep the lightbox when it is on. No database migration is required. Upgrade the Lace engine, admin and site packages together. Then adopt manually because lace.config.ts and site files are user-owned: raise the version of every model that allows image or gallery and run pnpm content:sync, which migrates stored image and gallery blocks without changing their data or settings; before the next site build run pnpm exec lace add block image gallery (or merge the new registry revisions into edited components), because older components fail with block_version_mismatch; copy the [data-lace-part="link"] rules from the starter stylesheet. See docs/lace-astro-site.md for the link field and the link part.

Template 0.33.0: deploy caching. The managed deploy/nginx.conf now serves the content-hashed files under /_astro/ (scripts, styles and image variants) with Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000, immutable (30 days) while pages keep revalidating, and refuses /_headers. docker-compose.yml gives the builder a persistent builder-cache volume at /cache for the pnpm store and the Astro image cache (cleared automatically above 2 GiB and after a failed build); the Cloudflare Pages workflow restores and saves the site's node_modules/.astro with actions/cache. No database migration and no API, admin, CLI, SDK or adapter change is required. Use the builder image of the same release and recreate the services with docker compose up -d builder web. Site files are user-owned, so adopt the Pages rule manually: copy site/public/_headers from a new starter project, or the snippet in docs/lace-astro-site.md, into the site's public/ directory. To reset the build cache, run docker compose rm --stop --force builder, remove the <project>_builder-cache volume and start the builder again.

Template 0.32.0: responsive images and the lightbox setting. Block images become WebP variants at 960 and 1920 px (each capped at the original width) with srcset, sizes, lazy loading and an inline blurred 64 px placeholder; animated GIFs become animated WebP. The built-in image block moves to version 3 and gallery to version 2, each with a boolean lightbox setting (default off) that opens the original full screen in a script-free <dialog>. No database migration is required. Upgrade the Lace engine, admin and site packages together. Then adopt manually because lace.config.ts and site files are user-owned: raise the version of every model that allows image or gallery and run pnpm content:sync, which migrates stored image and gallery blocks without changing their data; before the next site build run pnpm exec lace add block image gallery hero (or merge the new registry revisions into edited components), because older components fail with block_version_mismatch; add sharp to the site dependencies, set image: laceImageConfig(env) in site/astro.config.mjs (it allows only the public media path of LACE_API_BASE_URL) and copy the lightbox rules from the starter stylesheet. See docs/lace-astro-site.md for sizes, optimizeImages and the build caches.

Template 0.31.0: the managed deploy/nginx.conf now allows media uploads up to the API limit (previously nginx's 1 MiB default refused larger images with 413 before they reached the API). It declares client_max_body_size 1m for every request, matching the API's JSON body limit, and an exact location = /api/v1/admin/media with client_max_body_size 11m and proxy_request_buffering off, so uploads stream to the API and its own 10 MiB boundary decides. If you edited deploy/nginx.conf, the upgrade reports a conflict: merge those two directives and the media location by hand. Then recreate the web service with docker compose up -d web. Cloudflare projects are unaffected. No new API, admin, CLI or builder artifacts are required, and upgrade never edits .env, README, lace.config.ts or site files.

Template 0.30.0: alpha.6 release coordinates and paginated build export. Managed dependencies, image defaults and guide commands select 0.1.0-alpha.6. Generate the target with the same site mode/path and Cloudflare selection. Update all user-owned site Lace dependencies and API/builder image tags together; upgrade never edits .env, site files, lace.config.ts, README or Worker operator settings. Reinstall dependencies and rebuild the Worker/site. Coordinates become downloadable only after publication. Set LACE_API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/api:0.1.0-alpha.6 and LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/builder:0.1.0-alpha.6 in your user-owned .env explicitly.

Alpha.6 requires coordinated API, SDK, site and builder upgrades: the raw build-export endpoint returns version-bound pages with formatVersion 1. Direct HTTP consumers must follow nextCursor and handle BUILD_EXPORT_VERSION_CHANGED; the matching SDK assembles pages and retries once, while pinned builds fail on version mismatch. An older SDK can silently omit later pages; the new SDK rejects old exports without formatVersion. Public reads tolerate additive keys while retaining required-field, hidden-block and format safety.

Alpha.6 adds confirmed draft-media detachment requiring media:write and content:write. Published usage and more than 50 using entries are refused; each draft save is guarded and atomic, but earlier detachments remain after a later conflict. Refresh usage before retrying. Published snapshots and builds are unchanged. No new database migration exists relative to alpha.5; older baselines still require all pending journal migrations. Back up matching database, media, configuration and site before upgrade. Filesystem rollback does not restore detached values or deleted media; coordinated rollback may require restoring matching backups.

Template 0.29.0: alpha.5 release coordinates. Upgrade all @lacecms packages, create-lace and API/builder images together to 0.1.0-alpha.5 on npm channel next. Set LACE_API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/api:0.1.0-alpha.5 and LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/builder:0.1.0-alpha.5 in your user-owned .env; update @lacecms/astro, @lacecms/render, @lacecms/sdk and @lacecms/content to 0.1.0-alpha.5 in your Astro site. Review managed-file conflicts and preserve user-owned configuration and site source. Historical instructions below describe earlier transitions; their old package coordinates do not replace this target. Apply forward database migrations and content sync using the runtime-specific database instructions before adopting CE1–CE9 features. This upgrade does not publish or deploy anything.

Template 0.28.0 documents visual form layout metadata and creation-time slug suggestions in docs/lace-astro-site.md. Deploy matching content/config/contracts/API/admin before adopting optional layout/settingsLayout; no database migration or model/block version increase is required. Layout sync preserves content and revisions while advancing public version and requesting/coalescing a build. Older engines reject layout; remove options before rollback. lace.config.ts and site files remain user-owned.

Template 0.27.0: Gallery and Navigation blocks and a navigation global. @lacecms/content adds two built-in blocks defined with the group and list fields: gallery (an optional title and up to 50 images, each with media, an optional alt text and an optional caption that override the media item's) and navigation (an optional name read by screen readers and up to 20 links, each with a label, an optional URL and up to 20 submenu links). Both are edited with the generic group and list controls and need at least one image or link before publication. No database migration is required. Deploy the API, admin and site packages (@lacecms/sdk, @lacecms/render, @lacecms/astro, @lacecms/content) of the same release together: older content packages do not define builtInBlocks.gallery or builtInBlocks.navigation. New starter projects register all seven built-in blocks, allow them in home and posts (version 2), declare a navigation global (defineGlobal({ key: "navigation", version: 1, label: "Navigation", blocks: ["navigation"] })) and render its published blocks in the BaseLayout header with LaceBlocks, falling back to a static Home link until it is published; site/src/styles/global.css adds the gallery grid and the navigation layout. Because lace.config.ts and site files are yours, upgrade does not add them. To adopt them: run pnpm exec lace add block gallery navigation (add --site <path> for a site outside site/) to install GalleryBlock.astro and NavigationBlock.astro and extend the block map; add builtInBlocks.gallery and builtInBlocks.navigation to blocks in lace.config.ts, list them in the blocks of each model that may use them and raise those model versions; add the navigation global; run configuration sync; publish Navigation in Admin; and render site.global("navigation") with LaceBlocks and a fallback in your layout, with the CSS from docs/lace-astro-site.md. Upgrade never edits .env, .env.local, .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, worker/wrangler.jsonc, README, lace.config.ts or site files.

Template 0.26.0: block anchors, classes, settings and hidden blocks. Every stored block now carries an envelope beside its data: an optional in-page anchor (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique within the entry), an optional CSS class name, a hidden flag and the settings its definition declares with defineBlock({ settings }) (select, boolean, number or text fields, each with a defaultValue; built-in blocks declare none). Hidden blocks stay stored and publishable but are never delivered: public responses and the build export leave them out, and the render core skips them. Block components receive anchor, className and typed settings props from @lacecms/render; place id={anchor} on the component's root element and merge className into its class (for example class:list={["hero", className]}), as the new built-in components do (see docs/lace-astro-site.md). Invalid anchors, class names or settings fail the build with invalid_block_envelope. Breaking for user-written block migrations: a step now receives { data, settings } and returns { data, settings? } instead of bare data, so 2: ({ quote, ...rest }) => ({ ...rest, text: quote }) becomes 2: ({ data: { quote, ...rest } }) => ({ data: { ...rest, text: quote } }); configuration sync reports a step that still returns bare data as BLOCK_MIGRATION_INVALID. Deploy the API, admin and site packages (@lacecms/sdk, @lacecms/render, @lacecms/astro, @lacecms/content) of the same release together: older SDKs reject public blocks that carry the envelope. Requires migration 0009 (see the database steps). Block sources stay yours: upgrade never changes site files. To adopt the anchor and class support of the built-in components, run pnpm exec lace add block --all (add --site <path> for a site outside site/); unchanged components are updated, and edited ones are reported as conflicts to update by hand from the --write-new proposal. Scaffolded custom block components are never rewritten: add anchor and className to their props and root element yourself. Components that ignore the new props keep rendering, without ids or editor classes. Upgrade never edits .env, .env.local, .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, worker/wrangler.jsonc, README, lace.config.ts or site files.

Template 0.25.0: search and social metadata. Pages and collections opt into a per-entry SEO group with seo: true, or seo: { description: "<text or textarea field>", image: "<media field>" } to name fallback fields, in lace.config.ts; enabling or disabling SEO is structural, so raise the model version and run configuration sync (disabling it on a model with stored values needs the temporary removedSeo: true hint). One global may map site-wide defaults from its own fields with seoDefaults: { siteName, titleTemplate?, description?, image? }. The site SDK resolves fallbacks with site.seo(entry): the SEO title, otherwise the entry title through the title template (default %s | {siteName}); the SEO description, then the mapped field, then the site default; the same chain for the image; the SEO canonical, otherwise LACE_BUILD_SITE_URL plus the path. @lacecms/astro adds the LaceSeo.astro head component (title, description, canonical, robots, Open Graph and twitter:card) and the sitemapResponse and robotsResponse helpers. Site builds read two optional settings: LACE_BUILD_SITE_URL (canonical URLs, og:url, sitemap.xml and the robots.txt Sitemap line; without it the build warns and writes no sitemap) and LACE_SITE_INDEXING (on by default; off marks every page noindex, nofollow and makes robots.txt disallow everything, for staging). The managed docker-compose.yml passes both to the builder and the managed Cloudflare Pages workflow reads them from repository variables; set them as Pages environment variables for a Git-connected project. lace.config.ts and site files are yours, so upgrade never changes them: to adopt the starter output, add seo to your models and seoDefaults with description and image fields to your settings global (raise each changed model version, then sync), render <LaceSeo seo={site.seo(entry)} /> in your layout's head instead of <title> (type="article" for posts), and add src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts and src/pages/robots.txt.ts as shown in docs/lace-astro-site.md. Nothing breaks without adoption. Upgrade the API, admin, builder and the site packages together.

Template 0.24.0: global models for site-wide content. defineGlobal({ key, version, label?, description?, fields?, blocks? }) in lace.config.ts declares a model with exactly one entry and no path, route or slug; configuration sync creates its entry, and Admin lists it in a new Site navigation group where it is saved, published, reverted and unpublished like a page (it cannot be deleted or duplicated). Publishing a global requests a site build because any page may show it. The public API adds GET /api/v1/public/globals/:modelKey and the build export adds a globals key; site code reads a published global with site.global(key), which returns undefined until it is published (see docs/lace-astro-site.md). Deploy the API, admin and site packages (@lacecms/sdk, @lacecms/render, @lacecms/astro, @lacecms/content) of the same release together: older SDKs reject an export that carries globals. Requires migration 0007 (see the database steps). New starter projects declare a settings global (siteName, tagline) and their BaseLayout renders a site header from it with static fallbacks; because lace.config.ts and site files are yours, upgrade does not add them. To adopt it, add the defineGlobal from a freshly generated lace.config.ts, run configuration sync, publish Site settings in Admin, pass site={site} from each page to BaseLayout and render site.global("settings") there. Upgrade never edits .env, .env.local, .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, worker/wrangler.jsonc, README, lace.config.ts or site files.

Template 0.23.0: resolved public media and the published-only public contract. Every /api/v1/public content response and the build export changed shape: an entry is now returned directly as { id, modelKey, path, slug?, title, fields, blocks, publishedAt } (no draft, published or model keys, no { entry, path } wrapper in lists), and each response carries a media dictionary keyed by media ID with { id, url, mimeType, width, height, alt, caption, focalPoint }. Deploy the API, admin and site packages (@lacecms/sdk, @lacecms/render, @lacecms/astro, @lacecms/content) of the same release together. Pages that use getSite() and LaceBlocks keep working unchanged; code that reads REST responses or the raw build export must read the new shape, and LaceClient.getAllCollection now returns { items, media }. PublishedEntry and PublishedSite add media(id) and image(id, usageAlt?), and block components receive image(mediaId, usageAlt?) with the effective alt text, width, height and a focal-point objectPosition; see docs/lace-astro-site.md.

Block sources stay yours: upgrade never changes site files. To adopt the new image and hero components (effective alt text, dimensions, focal point, media caption fallback), run pnpm exec lace add block image hero (add --site <path> for a site outside site/); unchanged components are updated, and edited ones are reported as conflicts to update by hand from the --write-new proposal. Older components keep rendering with mediaUrl.

The built-in image block is version 2 (alt text optional, identity migration). Before building the site with the new packages, raise the version of every model that allows image in your lace.config.ts and run configuration sync (Compose: pnpm content:sync with api and dispatcher stopped; Cloudflare: pnpm exec lace content sync --target cloudflare-remote --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, or pnpm cf:content:sync locally), because the render core refuses image blocks still stored at version 1. Requires migrations 0005 and 0006 (see the database steps). Upgrade never edits .env, .env.local, .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, worker/wrangler.jsonc, README, lace.config.ts or site files.

Template 0.22.0: invitations, password recovery and account self-service. Administrators now invite people from Users (email and role) instead of setting their passwords; POST /api/v1/admin/users is removed, so deploy the API and admin artifacts together. Every user gets an Account page (display name, password, sessions) and the sign-in screen links to password reset. Outgoing account email stays optional: when LACE_EMAIL_PROVIDER is not configured or delivery fails, the invitation or reset dialog shows its link once so the administrator can pass it on. No new environment variables. Requires migration 0004_account_tokens (see the database steps). Upgrade never edits .env, .env.local, .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, worker/wrangler.jsonc, README, lace.config.ts or site files; see docs/lace-operations.md#accounts-and-invitations.

Template 0.21.0: optional transactional email and server-derived admin permissions. Email is optional and no database migration is added. Managed .env.example, the Compose API environment, worker/.dev.vars.example (local log provider) and the guides document LACE_EMAIL_PROVIDER (smtp, resend, cloudflare or development-only log), LACE_EMAIL_FROM and the provider settings; see docs/lace-operations.md#email-delivery. Deploy compatible API and admin artifacts together: the admin now reads its permissions from GET /api/v1/admin/session. Upgrade never edits .env, .env.local, .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, worker/wrangler.jsonc, README, lace.config.ts or site files: add email variables to your .env, or for the Worker add vars and secrets (and an optional send_email binding) to worker/wrangler.jsonc yourself. Check delivery with Admin Settings > Send test email.

Template 0.20.0: coordinated backup/restore, rotation and operator observation guidance. Deploy coherent alpha.4 API, contracts and admin artifacts together: Settings now displays the running CMS release. This is not a new database migration. Back up database, object bytes and configuration at one quiescent point; SQL-only restore is insufficient. Review docs/lace-operations.md. Preserve user-owned configuration, environment, README and Astro files; restore into an isolated origin with replacement secrets and disabled production hooks before validation. Local simulator evidence does not certify remote D1/R2 restore.

Template 0.19.0: trusted transport/proxy client identity and actor-scoped upload/token limits. Add LACE_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS to your user-owned .env only for controlled ingress proxy CIDRs; empty retains conservative peer-based protection. See docs/lace-compose-production.md. Host migrate, sync/check and bootstrap now refuse live Compose database consumers before opening SQLite; stop api and dispatcher throughout maintenance and restore Docker inspection if it fails. The source-only builder can remain running. See docs/lace-operations.md. No database migration is added. Previous template instructions remain applicable.

Template 0.18.0: release coordinates for Lace 0.1.0-alpha.4. This candidate corrects WCAG AA text contrast in failed-build details and restores sign-in recovery after editor mutation session loss while preserving unsaved-change confirmation. It also adds local cross-runtime verification. No new database migration is required beyond the alpha.3 baseline. Generate the target template with the same site mode/path and Cloudflare selection as your project.

Upgrade never edits your .env, .env.local, .lace/cloudflare-operator.env, README, lace.config.ts, worker/wrangler.jsonc or site source. Set LACE_API_IMAGE and LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE in .env to ghcr.io/lacecms/api:0.1.0-alpha.4 and ghcr.io/lacecms/builder:0.1.0-alpha.4 (or compatible overrides); in starter projects run pnpm --dir site add @lacecms/astro@0.1.0-alpha.4 @lacecms/render@0.1.0-alpha.4 @lacecms/sdk@0.1.0-alpha.4 @lacecms/content@0.1.0-alpha.4, and in existing-site mode update those packages in your site, then run pnpm install. Coordinates are downloadable only after explicit owner publication. Historical database guidance above still applies when upgrading from alpha.2.

Template 0.17.0: release coordinates for Lace 0.1.0-alpha.3. Managed files now name 0.1.0-alpha.3: the root package.json Lace dependencies, the LACE_API_IMAGE and LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE defaults in .env.example (ghcr.io/lacecms/api:0.1.0-alpha.3 and ghcr.io/lacecms/builder:0.1.0-alpha.3) and the versioned commands and prerequisites in the managed guides. This release carries the alpha.2 field-trial fixes: block order on save, builder source diagnostics, weak build-export ETags, the seven-status build history with Cloudflare Pages deployment tracking, explicit Cloudflare credentials with preflight, and the scenario guides. The managed docs/lace-compose-production.md no longer runs doctor's ready stage against the running stack (the API keeps SQLite in write-ahead-log mode, which doctor reports as unavailable); it checks docker compose ps and /health/ready instead. Generate the target template with your project's site mode/path and with --cloudflare exactly when your project has Cloudflare files.

Alpha.2 credential migration is manual: move CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN to the private file, remove its assignments from BOTH root .env and .env.local, clear the inherited token, and run lace cloudflare preflight --target cloudflare-remote --wrangler-auth oauth --operator-env .lace/cloudflare-operator.env. Unsetting a shell token alone does not prevent Wrangler reloading dotenv. Preflight verifies only credential selection and read-only D1 access; run the project-pinned wrangler whoami and review operation permissions before deploy or secret commands. A single sufficiently scoped token can instead be loaded explicitly for the intended Wrangler invocation. No credential, resource or deployment is changed by upgrade.

Template 0.9.0 (included when upgrading from 0.8.0 or earlier):

Template 0.9.0: new projects load and render published content through the @lacecms/sdk, @lacecms/render and @lacecms/astro packages with user-owned block components. Upgrade updates only managed files (the operations guide and the new docs/lace-astro-site.md); it never changes, adds or deletes files under site/.
Your site keeps building with its current files. To migrate it manually: generate a fresh 0.9.0 project in a temporary directory with the same create-lace version and compare its site/ with yours.
1. Add @lacecms/astro, @lacecms/render and @lacecms/content next to @lacecms/sdk in site/package.json at the release version, then run pnpm install.
2. Copy site/src/lib/lace.ts, site/src/env.d.ts, site/src/lace/blocks.ts, site/lace.site.json and site/src/components/lace/ from the fresh project.

3. Re-apply your own markup changes from site/src/components/*Block.astro to the matching files in site/src/components/lace/; the new components receive validated data instead of reading block fields themselves. Keep the data-lace-* hooks your styles use.

4. Change each page to call getSite() from src/lib/lace.ts, read entries with byPath('/'), entries('posts') and bySlug('posts', slug), render them with LaceBlocks from @lacecms/astro/LaceBlocks.astro and the blocks map, and type layouts with PublishedEntry from @lacecms/sdk.

5. Delete site/src/lib/site-data.ts, site/src/lib/rendering.ts, site/src/lib/rich-text.ts, site/src/components/BlockRenderer.astro, the RichText*.astro components and the old block components, then run pnpm typecheck and pnpm build.

Rich text and URLs are now validated with the CMS rules: content the old site copy accepted but the CMS rejects (such as https:example.com or a paragraph inside a paragraph) fails the build with its model, entry, block and field. To connect an existing Astro site instead of the starter, follow docs/lace-astro-site.md.
